prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same bug in `pre_parse_json` (src/mcp/server/mcpserver/utilities/func_metadata.py): the original check `field_info.annotation is not str` causes any string parameter whose annotation is a union containing `str` (e.g. `str | None`) to be run through `json.loads`, silently corrupting plain string values that happen to parse as valid JSON. #2032 introduces `_should_pre_parse_json` with a `_SIMPLE_TYPES` frozenset ({str, int, float, bool, NoneType}) and skips pre-parsing when every union member is one of those simple types (covers str|None, str|int, str|bool, etc.), but it checks union args via raw `in _SIMPLE_TYPES` membership, so a member like `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)]` (not equal to the bare `str` type object) is not recognized as simple, and pre-parsing still fires — leaving the corruption bug in place for the very common `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` parameter pattern. #3056 introduces `_unwrap_annotated` and `_is_optional_str`, explicitly stripping `Annotated[...]` before checking if a union member is `str`, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` as well as bare `str | None`. #3056's scope is narrower (only the str|None shape, not str|int/str|bool unions #2032 also covers), but it closes the specific corruption path involving Annotated-wrapped optional strings that #2032 misses. prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` checks union args via `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES`, which does not unwrap `Annotated[...]`, so the common `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` parameter shape (any optional string param with a description) still falls through to JSON pre-parsing and can still be corrupted — the exact bug #2032 was written to fix. #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` specifically to strip `Annotated` before the str-check, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for both bare `str | None` and `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None`. #3056 is narrower in type-union coverage (no generic handling of str|int/str|bool combinations), but it resolves the realistic Annotated case that #2032 leaves open.

members.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
members.author: adityuhkapoor
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3056: Both fix the same bug in `pre_parse_json` (src/mcp/server/mcpserver/utilities/func_metadata.py): the original check `field_info.annotation is not str` causes any string parameter whose annotation is a union containing `str` (e.g. `str | None`) to be run through `json.loads`, silently corrupting plain string values that happen to parse as valid JSON. #2032 introduces `_should_pre_parse_json` with a `_SIMPLE_TYPES` frozenset ({str, int, float, bool, NoneType}) and skips pre-parsing when every union member is one of those simple types (covers str|None, str|int, str|bool, etc.), but it checks union args via raw `in _SIMPLE_TYPES` membership, so a member like `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)]` (not equal to the bare `str` type object) is not recognized as simple, and pre-parsing still fires — leaving the corruption bug in place for the very common `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` parameter pattern. #3056 introduces `_unwrap_annotated` and `_is_optional_str`, explicitly stripping `Annotated[...]` before checking if a union member is `str`, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` as well as bare `str | None`. #3056's scope is narrower (only the str|None shape, not str|int/str|bool unions #2032 also covers), but it closes the specific corruption path involving Annotated-wrapped optional strings that #2032 misses.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 is the smaller, more targeted change: it edits only the bail-out branch, checks isinstance(..., JSONRPCRequest) so notifications aren't mishandled, and removes the pre-existing `# pragma: no cover` on that branch (implying it's now covered by a test). #3098's approach is more invasive — raising through the anyio task group requires a new recursive exception-unwrapping helper to recover the error from an ExceptionGroup, which affects the whole session/connect path rather than just the stuck request — and its diff also carries an unrelated import-style revert (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` -> `from __future__ import annotations`) that has nothing to do with the fix, adding unrelated churn and merge-conflict surface.

members.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both target the same bail-out branch in _handle_reconnection() when MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS is exceeded. Previously that branch just logged at debug level and returned silently, leaving the original request's caller awaiting a response that would never arrive. #2395 fixes it by constructing a JSONRPCError and sending it on ctx.read_stream_writer so the specific pending request (matched by ctx.session_message.message.id) unblocks with an error. #3098 fixes it by raising a StreamableHTTPError from the same path, then adds a recursive _unwrap_exception() helper to dig that error back out of the ExceptionGroup anyio wraps it in, so it propagates to the caller of the streamablehttp_client() context manager instead. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: #3041 splits the ENTIRE header into top-level segments first, then explicitly matches the segment whose leading token equals the target scheme ('bearer') before collecting its params via _extract_bearer_auth_params. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only does header.find(' ') once and treats everything after the first space as one flat param list, so for a multi-challenge header (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer error="y"') it would merge params from unrelated schemes together instead of isolating the Bearer challenge. #3041's approach directly targets the 'substring/scheme matching' failure mode named in its own title, while #3012 only solves the quoted-comma splitting piece and leaves the multi-scheme case unhandled.

members.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
members.author: adityuhkapoor
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3056: Both fix the same bug in `pre_parse_json` (src/mcp/server/mcpserver/utilities/func_metadata.py): the original check `field_info.annotation is not str` causes any string parameter whose annotation is a union containing `str` (e.g. `str | None`) to be run through `json.loads`, silently corrupting plain string values that happen to parse as valid JSON. #2032 introduces `_should_pre_parse_json` with a `_SIMPLE_TYPES` frozenset ({str, int, float, bool, NoneType}) and skips pre-parsing when every union member is one of those simple types (covers str|None, str|int, str|bool, etc.), but it checks union args via raw `in _SIMPLE_TYPES` membership, so a member like `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)]` (not equal to the bare `str` type object) is not recognized as simple, and pre-parsing still fires — leaving the corruption bug in place for the very common `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` parameter pattern. #3056 introduces `_unwrap_annotated` and `_is_optional_str`, explicitly stripping `Annotated[...]` before checking if a union member is `str`, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` as well as bare `str | None`. #3056's scope is narrower (only the str|None shape, not str|int/str|bool unions #2032 also covers), but it closes the specific corruption path involving Annotated-wrapped optional strings that #2032 misses.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 is the smaller, more targeted change: it edits only the bail-out branch, checks isinstance(..., JSONRPCRequest) so notifications aren't mishandled, and removes the pre-existing `# pragma: no cover` on that branch (implying it's now covered by a test). #3098's approach is more invasive — raising through the anyio task group requires a new recursive exception-unwrapping helper to recover the error from an ExceptionGroup, which affects the whole session/connect path rather than just the stuck request — and its diff also carries an unrelated import-style revert (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` -> `from __future__ import annotations`) that has nothing to do with the fix, adding unrelated churn and merge-conflict surface.

members.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both target the same bail-out branch in _handle_reconnection() when MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS is exceeded. Previously that branch just logged at debug level and returned silently, leaving the original request's caller awaiting a response that would never arrive. #2395 fixes it by constructing a JSONRPCError and sending it on ctx.read_stream_writer so the specific pending request (matched by ctx.session_message.message.id) unblocks with an error. #3098 fixes it by raising a StreamableHTTPError from the same path, then adds a recursive _unwrap_exception() helper to dig that error back out of the ExceptionGroup anyio wraps it in, so it propagates to the caller of the streamablehttp_client() context manager instead. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: #3041 splits the ENTIRE header into top-level segments first, then explicitly matches the segment whose leading token equals the target scheme ('bearer') before collecting its params via _extract_bearer_auth_params. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only does header.find(' ') once and treats everything after the first space as one flat param list, so for a multi-challenge header (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer error="y"') it would merge params from unrelated schemes together instead of isolating the Bearer challenge. #3041's approach directly targets the 'substring/scheme matching' failure mode named in its own title, while #3012 only solves the quoted-comma splitting piece and leaves the multi-scheme case unhandled.
